Authors: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.09.003
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43044650



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0. RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

Authors: Dimitrelou P, Alonaris E, Sergounioti A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70584
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43046504



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the biology of Nanosynbacter lyticus strain TM7x and critically assess its proposed relevance to periodontal disease. METHODS: This narrative review integrates foundational cultivation studies with a targeted PubMed update conducted on 29 October 2026. Human observational findings are distinguished from experimental evidence and from results concerning other Saccharibacteria. RESULTS: TM7x is an ultrasmall, genome-reduced episymbiont whose replication requires a compatible bacterial host. Studies of its interaction with Schaalia odontolytica XH001 reveal host adaptation, specialised pili, metabolic activity during transmission and changes in host physiology. Human disease associations frequently concern broader Saccharibacteria taxa and vary with population, sampling site and analytical method. Experimental studies demonstrate reduced inflammatory responses and, for several epibiont-host pairs, reduced bone loss in mice. These effects are context-dependent and do not establish clinical protection. Detailed knowledge of the species remains concentrated on the reference strain. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not establish TM7x as a causative human periodontal pathogen. It supports a model of context-dependent microbial and immune modulation, with unresolved consequences for human disease.

Authors: Huang JL, Li LJ, Wang ML, Zhu JQ, Dou LZ, Zhang X, Liu YM, Ke Y, Zhao YD, Wang JH, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71067
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43046223



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) system for standardized Ni classification of nasopharyngeal narrow-band imaging (NBI) and to evaluate whether AI assistance improves physician diagnostic consistency and biopsy-related decision making in a reader-study setting. METHODS: In this multicenter diagnostic study, 5404 high-quality nasopharyngeal NBI images were retrospectively collected. Lesion segmentation and five-class Ni classification networks were trained independently. Performance was evaluated in an internal test set, two independent external cohorts, and a recorded-video validation set. A prospective randomized multi-reader crossover study involving 12 physicians and 200 images from CHSZCAMS assessed the effect of AI assistance on diagnostic performance, inter-observer agreement, and potentially unnecessary biopsy decisions. RESULTS: In the two external cohorts, the model achieved accuracies of 0.889 and 0.873, with AUCs of 0.976 and 0.967, respectively. In recorded-video validation, accuracy was 0.888 and AUC was 0.974. AI assistance improved Fleiss kappa from 0.610 to 0.788 in junior physicians and from 0.744 to 0.870 in senior physicians (both p < 0.05). Potentially unnecessary biopsy decisions decreased from 21.6% to 10.3% in junior physicians and from 13.7% to 8.0% in senior physicians. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted Ni classification showed consistent diagnostic performance across validation cohorts and improved physician agreement across experience levels. In this reader-study setting, AI assistance reduced potentially unnecessary biopsy decisions, supporting further evaluation as a second-reader tool for nasopharyngeal NBI interpretation.

Authors: Budach V, Werner J, Wittlinger M, Fietkau R, Iro H, Engenhart-Cabillic R, Hautmann MG, Strutz J, Koelbl O, Flentje M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.060
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43044775



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the standard for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). For cisplatin (CDDP)-ineligible patients, mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil (MMC/5-FU) is the most common alternative, but randomized comparisons are lacking. We compared MMC/5-FU with CDDP/5-FU as concurrent partners of hyperfractionated-accelerated radiotherapy (HART) in unresectable, locally advanced HNSCC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this multicenter phase III trial, 364 patients with stage IVA/IVB (UICC TNM 6th edition) oropharyngeal or hypopharyngeal HNSCC were randomized 1:1 to HART (72 Gy/6 weeks) plus either weekly CDDP 30 mg/m² (n=182) or MMC 10 mg/m² on days 5 and 36 (n=182), both with continuous-infusion 5-FU 600 mg/m²/d on days 1-5. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints included freedom from progression (FFP), freedom from distant metastasis (FFDM), local, regional and locoregional control, and toxicity, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and, post hoc, in a competing-risk framework. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 87 months, CDDP/5-FU was not superior for OS (10-year OS 23% vs. 18%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.89, 95% CI 0.69-1.15; log-rank p=0.418). In the competing-risk analysis, CDDP/5-FU reduced distant metastasis (5-year cumulative incidence 25.9% vs. 36.1%; subdistribution HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96; p=0.031) and progression (45.6% vs. 56.3%; subdistribution HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.98; p=0.037). Kaplan-Meier estimates were directionally consistent but not significant (10-year FFDM 66% vs. 52%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.02; p=0.060; FFP HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.59-1.05); local, regional and locoregional control (HR 0.80-1.01) and toxicity profiles did not differ. Serum creatinine (p<0.001) and the AE/SAE rate (24.2% vs. 15.4%; p=0.048) were higher with CDDP. CONCLUSION: ARO 04-01/AHMO did not show superiority of CDDP/5-FU over MMC/5-FU for overall survival. CDDP-based CRT remains the established standard for fit patients; MMC/5-FU is a safe and effective alternative with comparable overall survival and measurably lower nephrotoxicity and cumulative AE/SAE burden for CDDP-contraindicated patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: DRKS00040575.

Authors: Salans M, Yom SS, Dufault SM, Mowery YM, Spasojevic I, Chan JW, Zhen W, Penchev S, Harehdasht SA, MacLeod D, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.11.001
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43044774



Abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: MnTnBuOE-2-PyP5+ (BMX-001) is a manganese metalloporphyrin superoxide dismutase mimic that inhibits radiation stress-induced pathways and may mitigate treatment-related side effects. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of BMX-001 on severe oral mucositis (OM), xerostomia, dermatitis, quality of life, and patient reported outcomes (PROs) among patients undergoing chemoradiation for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). MATERIALS/METHODS: This multicenter, phase I/II trial included patients with stage III-IVB HNSCC (AJCC 7th ed) undergoing definitive or postoperative chemoradiation (CRT). Patients received a subcutaneous BMX-001 loading dose followed by twice-weekly maintenance dosing through one week post-CRT at three loading/maintenance dose levels (7/3.5 mg, 14/7 mg, and 28/14 mg), with level 3 expanded for phase II endpoints. OM, xerostomia, and dermatitis were assessed weekly during treatment, within one month, and at six and 12 months post-chemoradiation. PROs and saliva production (stimulated and unstimulated) were measured at baseline, end of CRT, and one, six and 12 months post-CRT. Descriptive statistics summarized adverse events, symptom duration, and PROs. RESULTS: Between 5/2017 and 12/2019, 29 patients were enrolled; 86% had oropharynx primaries (n=25; n=24 HPV+) and 89.7% (n=26) underwent definitive CRT. One patient experienced two serious adverse events possibly related to BMX-001. Grade 3 OM occurred in 41.4% (n=12); acute and chronic grade ≥2 xerostomia occurred in 17.9% (n=5) and 9.1% (n=2), respectively, and 6.9% (n=2) experienced grade 3 dermatitis. At a median follow-up of 24 months, 96.6% were alive without progression. In exploratory longitudinal analyses of the 23 patients treated at the recommended phase II dose, patient-reported symptom and quality-of-life measures generally worsened at the end of CRT and subsequently improved. Several measures were no longer statistically different from baseline by six months, while measures of xerostomia remained elevated. CONCLUSIONS: BMX-001 is safe and feasible in patients with advanced HNSCC. In addition, BMX-001 shows promising efficacy for mitigating CRT-associated toxicity and warrants further study in larger, controlled trials.

Authors: Clark AS, Omene C, Yau C, Wallace AM, Stringer-Reasor E, Chien AJ, Isaacs C, Han HS, Albain KS, Boughey JC, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108643
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43044269



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preclinical evidence suggests synergy between poly-ADP-ribose inhibitors and camptothecin chemotherapy. We tested the talazoparib and irinotecan combination (TI) in the neoadjuvant setting in the I-SPY2 trial in patients with HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: I-SPY2 is a phase II platform trial for stage 2/3 early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. Participants were adaptively randomized to one of several experimental neoadjuvant therapies or control based on receptor subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR), HER2 status, and MammaPrint risk (MP1, MP2). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). Treatments 'graduate' if/when they achieve an 85% Bayesian probability of success in a subtype-specific phase III trial. Only HER2-negative patients were eligible for randomization to the TI arm. All patients received weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, followed by doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide and surgery. Participants randomized to the TI arm received daily oral talazoparib and irinotecan infusions every other week. Pathway-specific biomarkers were assessed for response prediction. RESULTS: The combination of talazoparib and irinotecan failed to graduate from the I-SPY2 trial, with a 19% modeled posterior probability of pCR in the TI arm compared with 20% in the control arm among all patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. The most common adverse events were neutropenia and anemia in the TI arm and neuropathy and fatigue in the control arm. pCR rates were highest in patients with germline Breast Cancer Gene 1 or 2 (BRCA1/2) mutations receiving TI (pCR rate 50%) and in those with tumors expressing a DNA repair deficiency signature. CONCLUSIONS: TI will not be further explored as a combination given lack of improved efficacy over control (paclitaxel) for neoadjuvant treatment in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. pCR rates were highest (50%) among patients with germline BRCA1/2 mutations, likely due to the efficacy of talazoparib alone. Further combinations could be explored in patients with HER2-negative breast cancer and a germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 mutation.

Authors: Asamnew A, Shure W, Asres MS, Wondimeneh Y, Ferede G, Gelaw B, Gelaw A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357953
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043898



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza A virus is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections and contributes substantially to the global disease burden. Laboratory-confirmed data on influenza A virus infection remain limited in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of influenza A virus infection and to identify possible associated factors among patients with acute respiratory tract infections attending selected health institutions in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia. METHODS: A multi-center, health facility-based cross-sectional study was carried out from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. In total, 490 patients with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled from five health facilities in Gondar City. Demographic, behavioral, and clinical information was collected using a structured questionnaire. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and tested for influenza A virus using multiplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with influenza A virus infection. RESULTS: Influenza A virus was detected in 65 of the 490 participants, with an overall prevalence of 13.3% (95% CI: 10.3-16.3). Among the confirmed cases, 48 (73.8%) were A(H1N1) and 17 (26.2%) were A(H3N2). In multivariable logistic regression, participants aged 5-17 years (AOR: 3.14; 95% CI: 1.36-7.25; p = 0.008) and 18-49 years (AOR: 3.50; 95% CI: 1.54-7.20; p = 0.002) had higher odds of infection than those aged <5 years. Secondary education was associated with lower odds of infection compared with no formal education (AOR: 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.75; p = 0.029), while employed participants had higher odds than students (AOR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.47-7.80; p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Influenza A virus infection was detected among patients presenting with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, highlighting the importance of influenza surveillance and laboratory confirmation in this population. Strengthening routine molecular surveillance, promoting seasonal influenza vaccination among high-risk populations, reinforcing infection prevention and control measures, and implementing targeted community health education are essential to improve influenza prevention and control.

Authors: Wiener RC, Waters C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362482
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043884



Abstract:
Over the last decade trampoline use has increased. Many injuries occur that require emergency department (ED) care. The purpose of this research is to examine the role of age in trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries that require ED care. Data from the 2024 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) was used. Trampoline-related injuries were extracted from the data set. Oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries were compared with other types of trampoline-related injuries by age groups (0 to <6 years, 6 to <12 years, and 12 to ≤18 years) in Chi-Square analyses and logistic regression analyses. There were 3548 NEISS-reported trampoline-associated injuries for children, ages 0 to ≤18 years, in 2024. This corresponded to an estimated 101,474 trampoline injuries in the United States in 2024. Of these, 21.7% were oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries (weighted estimate of 22,033 injuries). Of all the trampoline-related injuries in children ages 0 to ≤18 years, children ages 0 to <6 years had 33.0% of the injuries; children ages 6 to <12 years had 51.9%; and, children ages 12 to ≤18 years had 15.1%. Children ages 0 to <6 years had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.66 [95% CI: 1.11, 2.50; p = 0.0155] compared with children ages 12 to ≤18 years for oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries as compared with other injuries from trampolines. Younger children have significantly higher odds of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries requiring emergency department care compared with adolescents, supporting age as an important host factor within the Haddon Matrix framework. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and anticipatory guidance for younger children.

Authors: Kajiura S, Nakamura N, Hayashi R
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10829-1
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43043384



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) in head and neck cancer can return tumor-agnostic and histology-associated signals, but practical benchmarks for reported ERBB2 amplification and residual non-immune-checkpoint-inhibitor (non-ICI) scenario-based genomic signal coverage are limited. We quantified the contribution of ERBB2 amplification and ALK fusion/rearrangement in nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) data, focusing on salivary gland tumors and salivary duct carcinoma. METHODS: This retrospective descriptive scenario-based analysis included anonymized C-CAT-derived head and neck CGP-tested cases. Overall and residual non-ICI frameworks were assessed before ERBB2, after adding reported ERBB2 amplification, and after adding ALK fusion/rearrangement as an updated 2026 layer. RESULTS: The cohort included 3,089 cases. In the overall framework, scenario-based genomic signal coverage increased from 280/3,089 (9.1%) to 501/3,089 (16.2%) after adding reported ERBB2 amplification (+ 221 cases; +7.2% points). In the residual non-ICI framework, the increase was from 61/3,089 (2.0%) to 309/3,089 (10.0%) (+ 248 cases; +8.0% points). Reported ERBB2 amplification was detected in 249/3,089 (8.1%), and the descriptive ERBB2 union in 379/3,089 (12.3%). In salivary duct carcinoma, reported ERBB2 amplification occurred in 105/262 (40.1%), the descriptive ERBB2 union in 124/262 (47.3%), and residual non-ICI post-ERBB2 framework positivity in 114/262 (43.5%). ALK fusion/rearrangement added 0 cases. CONCLUSION: Reported ERBB2 amplification materially increased scenario-based genomic signal coverage in head and neck cancer, especially salivary duct carcinoma. These findings provide an implementation-level benchmark for CGP counseling and expert-panel discussion in head and neck oncology.

Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-1545
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43043002



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate post-treatment assessment after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC) remains challenging due to limitations of standard imaging. We evaluated the diagnostic performance, prognostic value and optimal timing of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for molecular residual disease (MRD) detection. METHODS: Seventy-four patients with LA-HNSCC treated with definitive CRT were prospectively enrolled. Plasma samples were collected before treatment, at 8 and 12 weeks after CRT, and during follow-up. ctDNA was analysed using a plasma-only methylation-based assay. Diagnostic performance for recurrence detection and associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated and compared with 12-week PET/CT findings. RESULTS: Baseline ctDNA was detectable in 85.1% of patients. Among post-treatment timepoints, week-12 ctDNA showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for recurrence detection, with 69% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% positive predictive value, and 76% negative predictive value. Detectable week-12 ctDNA was associated with shorter PFS (HR, 6.44; 95% CI, 2.73-16.74; p<0.001) and OS (HR, 7.31; 95% CI, 2.80-22.31; p<0.001 ). Longitudinal ctDNA surveillance identified additional recurrences among patients with initially undetectable week-12 ctDNA. Exploratory analyses integrating PET/CT and ctDNA identified prognostically distinct PFS groups (log-rank P=0.033), with the greatest additional prognostic stratification observed among PET partial-responders. CONCLUSIONS: Plasma-only methylation-based ctDNA provided high-specificity prognostic information after definitive CRT in LA-HNSCC, particularly at week 12 and in PET partial-responders. ctDNA may complement PET/CT for post-treatment risk stratification, but should not be used as a stand-alone test to exclude recurrence.
